comparisons.peer_topic: Embedded segment net revenue and drivers for fiscal year 2024
comparisons.peer_summary: Embedded net revenue decreased by 33% to $3.6 billion in 2024 from $5.3 billion in 2023, primarily due to lower demand as customers normalized inventory levels.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD disclose specific revenue drivers and volume trends for their respective core business segments in 2024, highlighting the impact of demand cycles and inventory normalization. NVDA emphasizes that its Compute & Networking demand 'is expected to remain concentrated,' indicating sustained strength in a specific high-growth area. In contrast, AMD reports a significant contraction in its Embedded segment, where net revenue 'decreased by 33%, compared to net revenue of $5.3 billion in 2023,' attributing this decline to 'lower demand as customers continued to normalize their inventory levels.' While NVDA highlights concentration and growth in AI infrastructure, AMD highlights a cyclic downturn and inventory correction in its embedded markets.

sentences.text: Our estimated Compute & Networking demand is expected to remain concentrated.
Embedded net revenue of $3.6 billion in 2024 decreased by 33%, compared to net revenue of $5.3 billion in 2023.
The decrease in net revenue was primarily due to lower demand as customers continued to normalize their inventory levels.

comparisons.peer_summary: International sales accounted for 66% of net revenue in 2024 (65% in 2023) and are expected to remain significant; substantially all sales transactions are denominated in U.S. dollars.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose the geographic concentration of their revenue as a key business driver. NVDA explicitly states that its estimated Compute & Networking demand 'is expected to remain concentrated,' implying a reliance on a specific subset of customers or sectors. AMD provides a broader geographic perspective, noting that 'International sales as a percentage of net revenue were 66% in 2024' and that 'We expect that international sales will continue to be a significant portion of total sales.' While NVDA's concentration refers to customer/sector density within its demand, AMD's disclosure quantifies the international share of its total sales, both serving as risk and driver disclosures regarding revenue concentration.

sentences.text: Our estimated Compute & Networking demand is expected to remain concentrated.
